West Virginia Squatters Rights and Adverse Possession FAQ

Can a squatter take ownership of my West Virginia house?

Check the statute and talk to a West Virginia attorney about your facts.

Can a squatter in West Virginia ever become the legal owner?

Yes, but only by meeting a long list of requirements for a full ten years. West Virginia does not have a short squatter statute. A person who occupies land and claims title relies on the doctrine of adverse possession, and the courts hold that person to a heavy burden of proof.

Ten years comes from W. Va. Code 55-2-1, which says no one may make an entry on land or bring an action to recover it except within ten years after the right first accrued to that person or to someone through whom they claim. When an owner waits too long to act against an occupant, the clock can matter. This page explains how the doctrine works, how it differs from a tenant who stays after a lease, and what an owner selling a house can do.

What must an adverse possessor prove?

The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals lists six elements. One who seeks title to a tract by adverse possession must prove each of them for the statutory period (Somon v. Murphy Fabrication & Erection Co., 160 W.Va. 84, 232 S.E.2d 524 (1977), repeated in Elder v. Smith (1996)).

  1. The land was held adversely or hostilely.
  2. The possession was actual.
  3. It was open and notorious, sometimes stated as visible and notorious.
  4. It was exclusive.
  5. It was continuous.
  6. It was under claim of title or color of title.

The statutory period is ten years. Missing any element defeats the claim.

The burden is also stricter than in an ordinary civil case. In Cobb v. Collins (2018), the Court repeated that the party claiming title by adverse possession must prove all essential elements by clear and convincing evidence, citing Brown v. Brown, 196 W.Va. 559, 474 S.E.2d 489 (1996).

What does "hostile" mean when someone occupies land?

Hostile means against the owner's right, not angry. In Elder v. Smith the Court explained that the claimant must show possession against the right of the true owner and inconsistent with the owner's title. The Court added that the word hostile is synonymous with adverse and does not require ill will or malevolence toward the owner.

That matters for an owner who gave permission. Someone staying in a relative's house with the owner's consent, or paying rent as a tenant, is not holding against the owner's right in the way the doctrine requires. We did not find a page that covers every permission scenario, so ask an attorney how a family arrangement or an informal handshake deal would be treated.

If a claimant does satisfy every element for more than ten years, the Court's syllabus point quoted in Cobb says actual, open, notorious, exclusive and continuous adverse possession for more than ten years confers good legal title, enabling the owner to maintain an action for unlawful entry and detainer against one who enters unlawfully (Harman v. Alt, 69 W.Va. 287, 71 S.E. 709 (1911)).

What is the difference between a squatter and a holdover tenant?

A tenant entered with the owner's permission under a lease or oral arrangement, so the landlord-tenant statutes apply. A squatter entered with no right at all. The remedies differ.

SituationMain legal routeSource
Tenant behind on rent, in breach, or damaging the propertyVerified petition in magistrate or circuit court; hearing 5 to 10 judicial days after filingW. Va. Code 55-3A-1
Occupant claiming title by long possessionAdverse possession doctrine; six elements, ten years, clear and convincing proof55-2-1; Somon; Cobb
Person on property without authority after being asked to leaveCriminal trespass in a structure: misdemeanor, fine up to $10061-3B-2(a)
Entering a structure posted as condemnedMisdemeanor, fine up to $100, jail up to six months, or both61-3B-2(b)

The summary route in Article 3A is written for tenants. It lets a person desiring to remove a tenant apply to the court, and a tenant who is served may raise any defense available in an ejectment or unlawful detainer action (55-3A-2). Whether a particular occupant is a tenant, a guest or a trespasser is a fact question, so get legal advice before acting.

What does West Virginia law say about trespass on a house?

Under W. Va. Code 61-3B-2(a), a person who knowingly enters a structure without being authorized, licensed or invited, or who is asked to leave by the owner, tenant or agent and refuses, is guilty of a misdemeanor, with a fine of not more than $100.

Subsection (b) is stronger for condemned buildings: a person who knowingly and willfully enters a structure with a clear posting that a municipal or county government has condemned it as unfit for human habitation faces a fine of not more than $100, up to six months in jail, or both. For a first violation the court may substitute community service or pretrial diversion. Subsection (c) carries heavier penalties when the offender is armed with a dangerous weapon and intends bodily injury.

A separate section, 61-3B-3, covers trespass on property other than a structure where notice against entering is given. The details depend on how notice is given, so read the section itself before posting land.

What should an owner do about an unauthorized occupant?

Act early, in writing, and through the proper channel. We are not lawyers, and the right step depends on whether the person is a tenant, a guest, or someone with no connection to you. These are practical points that follow from the statutes above.

  • Document when you last inspected the house and who had permission to be there.
  • If the person is asked to leave and refuses, the trespass statute refers to a request by the owner, tenant or agent, so keep a record of that request.
  • If the person paid or promised rent, treat the matter as a tenancy and use the Article 3A petition rather than self-help.
  • Do not wait years. Section 55-2-1 gives ten years for an action to recover land, and the adverse possession elements include continuous possession.
  • Talk to a West Virginia attorney before changing locks, shutting off utilities or removing belongings.

Vacant inherited houses are a common setup for these problems. A house sits empty after a death, the owner lives out of state, and months pass between visits. Checking the property regularly, keeping the taxes current and recording who holds title all make it harder for anyone to claim they were there openly and exclusively.

How does an occupant problem affect selling a West Virginia house?

It affects who can close and how fast. A buyer who plans to live in the house needs possession at closing. A traditional buyer with a mortgage will also have an appraiser and an inspector who need access, and a contested occupant can stall both.

If you own a house with a squatter, a holdover tenant or an unclear occupancy, you can still sell. We buy houses in West Virginia as-is, and we can discuss an offer on a property where someone is living without your agreement. We will not tell you the occupant has no rights, and you should not rely on us for that answer. The title question belongs to a court, and the practical timeline depends on which statute applies.

Before you list or accept an offer, assemble what you can: the deed, tax bills, any lease, texts or letters with the occupant, and photos showing the condition and date. These help whether you evict, negotiate a move-out or sell with the occupant in place.

More questions about West Virginia Squatters Rights and Adverse Possession

How long does adverse possession take in West Virginia?

Ten years. W. Va. Code 55-2-1 sets ten years for entering on or recovering land, and the Supreme Court of Appeals lists ten years as the statutory period for adverse possession. The claimant must also prove each of the six elements.

What standard of proof applies to an adverse possession claim?

Clear and convincing evidence. In Cobb v. Collins (2018) the Court repeated that the party claiming title by adverse possession bears the burden of proving all essential elements by clear and convincing evidence.

Does a squatter have to be hostile to the owner?

Hostile means possession against the owner's right and inconsistent with the owner's title. The Court said it does not require ill will or malevolence. Someone who has the owner's permission is not occupying against the owner's right in that sense.

Is trespassing in a house a crime in West Virginia?

Yes. Under 61-3B-2(a), knowingly entering a structure without authorization, or refusing to leave after being asked, is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than $100. Entering a structure posted as condemned carries a higher penalty.

Can I sell my house if someone is living there without permission?

You can sell the property, but possession is the practical issue. A buyer who needs to move in will want the occupant gone. A cash buyer who purchases as-is may be willing to take a house with an occupant, so ask for an offer and describe the situation honestly.

What the official sources say

  • On termination of the tenancy and within the applicable notice period, the landlord must deliver the security deposit minus deductions with a written itemization. (W. Va. Code 37-6A-2(a); source)
  • If damages exceed the deposit and need a third-party contractor, landlord gives written notice within the applicable notice period and then has an additional fifteen days to provide an itemization. (W. Va. Code 37-6A-2(c); source)

Which West Virginia laws cover landlords and tenants?

Three parts of the West Virginia Code do most of the work: Chapter 37, Article 6 (landlord and tenant), Chapter 37, Article 6A (residential rental security deposits) and Chapter 55, Article 3A (remedies for wrongful occupation of residential rental property). Together they cover repairs, deposits, notice to end a tenancy and the court route for removing a tenant.

If you own a rental you are thinking of selling, these are the rules the buyer inherits. They also decide how fast a tenant can be moved out if the sale needs an empty house.

  • Article 6 lists 31 sections, from transfer of the landlord's interest (37-6-1) to the habitability duty (37-6-30).
  • Article 6A has six sections: definitions, deposits, records, prohibited lease terms, landlord noncompliance and effective date.
  • Article 3A has three sections: the petition, defenses and the court proceeding.

What happens to a tenant's lease when the landlord sells the rental?

The lease does not disappear. Under W. Va. Code 37-6-1, a grantee or assignee of leased land, or of the reversion, can use the same conditions, forfeitures and lease covenants the original lessor could have used. Section 37-6-2 gives the tenant the matching benefit: a lessee may enforce the lease's conditions, covenants and promises against whoever takes the reversion, as if that person were the original lessor, except for warranties.

For a seller, that means a signed lease is part of what you are selling. A buyer takes the property subject to the tenant's rights, and the tenant can hold the new owner to the lease terms.

The deposit follows the property too. Section 37-6A-2(e) says whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends is bound by the deposit rules and must return any deposit that is duly owed to the tenant. That applies whether or not the deposit was handed over in the sale and regardless of any contract between the old and new landlord. If you sell a rental with a tenant in place, settle in writing who is carrying the deposit, because the tenant can look to the new owner.

How do security deposits work in West Virginia?

At the end of the tenancy and within the applicable notice period, the landlord must deliver the deposit, minus deductions, together with a written itemization (37-6A-2(a)). The statute limits what the landlord may deduct.

Allowed uses of the deposit under 37-6A-2(b):

  • Rent due, including reasonable late charges stated in the rental agreement.
  • Damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the rental agreement, less reasonable wear and tear.
  • Unpaid utilities that the landlord billed, paid and that the tenant owed under the agreement.
  • Reasonable costs to remove and store the tenant's personal property.
  • Other charges in the rental agreement, including a third-party contractor's repair of tenant damage.

When damages exceed the deposit and need an outside contractor, the landlord must give written notice within the notice period and then has an extra fifteen days to send the itemization and repair cost (37-6A-2(c)). Delivery can be personal or by mail to the last known or forwarding address. If a mailed deposit comes back undeliverable, the landlord holds it for six months and must hand it over within 72 hours of a written request (37-6A-2(g)).

What does a landlord owe in return for a tenant's rent?

West Virginia requires a landlord of residential property to deliver the unit fit and habitable and to keep it that way (W. Va. Code 37-6-30(a)(1)). The same subsection spells out the duties.

  • Meet applicable health, safety, fire and housing codes, unless the tenant, a family member or a guest caused the failure.
  • Keep common areas of multiple housing units clean, safe and in repair.
  • Make repairs needed to keep the premises fit, except those caused mainly by the tenant's lack of reasonable care.
  • Keep electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating and air-conditioning facilities in safe working order when the landlord supplies them.
  • In multiple units, provide for removal of garbage and waste.
  • Where units have direct public utility connections, supply running water, reasonable hot water, and reasonable heat from October 1 through the last day of April.

Two limits matter. A greater duty written into the rental agreement controls over the statute (37-6-30(b)). And the section does not require the landlord to make repairs while the tenant is in arrears on rent (37-6-30(c)). For an owner selling a rental, deferred repairs on a unit with a tenant in place can become a dispute, which is one reason some owners prefer a buyer who takes the property as it stands.

How does a landlord remove a tenant through the courts?

The landlord files a verified petition in magistrate court or circuit court in the county where the property sits (W. Va. Code 55-3A-1). The sheriff removes a tenant who stays past the date set in the court's order (55-3A-3(f)).

StepWhat the statute says
PetitionOwner or agent states the right to possession, describes the property and alleges rent arrears, breach of a warranty or lease covenant, or deliberate or negligent damage (55-3A-1(a))
Hearing dateCourt sets a hearing not less than five nor more than 10 judicial days after filing (55-3A-1(b))
NoticeServed under Rule 4 of the Rules of Civil Procedure or by certified mail, return receipt requested; tenant may file a written defense within five days of receiving it (55-3A-1(c))
No responseIf the tenant files nothing by the hearing, the court enters an order granting immediate possession (55-3A-3(a))
ContestedIf the tenant answers, the court holds a hearing; continuances are for cause only, and a tenant who gets one must pay periodic rent into court (55-3A-3(d))
OrderCourt sets the vacate time; if the tenant stays, the sheriff removes the tenant (55-3A-3(f))

A tenant may raise any defense available in an ejectment or unlawful detainer action (55-3A-2). In a rent case, a tenant who answers that the landlord breached a material covenant on which the duty to pay rent depends gets a hearing on that issue (55-3A-3(b)).

What can a landlord do with belongings left behind?

After a possession order, the landlord can dispose of property the tenant says in writing is abandoned, or of garbage, without liability (55-3A-3(h)(1)). Otherwise the landlord may remove and store the items, or leave them in place, and may dispose of them after thirty days if the tenant has not paid the reasonable costs and has not reclaimed them, or if storage costs equal the value of the goods.

If the property is worth more than $300 and the tenant or a secured party says they intend to collect it, the landlord must store it up to thirty more days, provided they pay reasonable storage and removal costs (55-3A-3(i)).

A different process applies when the tenant has simply left. Under 37-6-6, if a tenant who owes rent abandons the property, the landlord posts a written notice in a conspicuous place requiring payment within one month. If the rent is unpaid, the landlord gets possession and the tenant's right ends. Before disposing of belongings the landlord must post and mail a notice by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing, giving a removal date at least thirty days after mailing (sixty days if the tenant is on active military duty and has said so).

What can a tenant do if the landlord keeps the deposit?

If a landlord's noncompliance with Article 6A is willful or not in good faith, the tenant is entitled to a judgment for the unreturned deposit plus damages for annoyance or inconvenience equal to one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (37-6A-5(a)). When the tenant owes rent, the court credits that award against the rent due.

Civil actions under the article go to magistrate court or circuit court in the county where the rental sits (37-6A-5(b)).

TopicRuleCitation
Repair dutyFit and habitable at start and throughout37-6-30
HeatReasonable heat October 1 to April 30 where supplied by direct utility connection37-6-30(a)(7)
Extra time for itemization15 days after notice, when contractor needed37-6A-2(c)
Undeliverable depositHeld six months37-6A-2(g)
Penalty1.5 times the amount wrongfully withheld37-6A-5(a)
Court hearing5 to 10 judicial days after filing55-3A-1(b)

How do these rules affect selling a rental house in West Virginia?

They set the clock and the cost. A sale with a tenant in place carries the lease, the deposit and the repair duty to the buyer. A sale that needs vacant possession means going through the 55-3A court process first, and that depends on a valid ground such as unpaid rent or damage.

Owners who sell to us for cash can choose either route. We buy houses as-is, including rentals with tenants, and the offer is written for the situation you describe. Before you sign anything, check your lease, your deposit records and any notices you have served. Get advice from a West Virginia attorney or Legal Aid of West Virginia's renters' rights pages if a dispute is open. This page is general information, not legal advice.

More questions about West Virginia Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

Does a West Virginia tenant have to move out when the landlord sells the house?

No, not by reason of the sale alone. Under W. Va. Code 37-6-1 and 37-6-2, the buyer of the landlord's interest takes it subject to the lease, and the tenant can enforce the lease terms against the new owner. Ending the tenancy still follows the lease and the notice rules.

How long does a West Virginia landlord have to return a security deposit?

The deposit, minus lawful deductions and with a written itemization, is due on termination and within the applicable notice period (37-6A-2(a)). If damages exceed the deposit and need a contractor, the landlord gets an extra fifteen days after giving written notice to itemize the cost.

Can a landlord cut off heat or lock a tenant out in West Virginia?

The statutes we reviewed provide a court process for removal (55-3A), with the sheriff enforcing a possession order. Section 37-6-30 also requires reasonable heat from October 1 through April 30 where the landlord supplies it through a direct utility connection. Ask a West Virginia attorney about any specific lockout.

What is the penalty if a landlord wrongfully withholds a deposit?

If the noncompliance is willful or not in good faith, the tenant can recover the unreturned deposit plus damages of one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (37-6A-5(a)).

Can I sell a rental house with a tenant still living in it?

Yes. The lease and the deposit obligation travel with the property, so the buyer steps into the landlord's position. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can take a tenant-occupied house, and you can raise that when you ask for an offer.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a West Virginia Eviction Notice Rules sale

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Periodic tenancy under one year ends on notice of one full period (the no-cause route). (W. Va. Code 37-6-5; source)
Selling in West Virginia?
We buy West Virginia houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How does a West Virginia eviction start?

An eviction in West Virginia starts with a verified petition filed in the magistrate court or circuit court of the county where the rental is located. Section 55-3A-1 of the West Virginia Code lets an owner or the owner's agent apply for summary relief to remove a tenant from residential rental property.

The petition has to say four things: that the petitioner is the owner or agent and has a right to recover possession, a brief description of the property, the reason the tenant is wrongfully occupying it, and a request for possession. The reason must be one of three. The tenant is behind on rent, has breached a warranty or leasehold covenant, or has deliberately or negligently damaged the property or knowingly let someone else do so. The petition describes the arrearage, breach or act in question.

The West Virginia Judiciary publishes a petition form for this, titled Petition for Summary Relief, Wrongful Occupation of Residential Rental Property. It cites sections 55-3A-1, 50-5-8(a) and 37-15-3 and Magistrate Court Civil Rule 6A, and it needs to be sworn or affirmed before a notary.

What are the notice types and how many days apply?

The statute we read sets hearing and response periods in days, and it ties the no-cause route to the length of the tenancy. The table below lists the periods we confirmed in the Code and the court materials.

Step or noticeTime periodSource
Hearing after petition is filedNot less than 5 and not more than 10 judicial days after filing55-3A-1(b)
Tenant's written defenseWithin 5 days of receiving the notice of hearing55-3A-1(c)
Answer under magistrate rulesWithin 5 days after service of the summons and complaintMagistrate Court Civil Rule 4
Jury demandWritten notice within 5 days of serviceJudiciary petition form
Year-to-year tenancy, termination noticeIn writing, at least three months before the end of any year37-6-5
Periodic tenancy under one year, no-cause noticeNotice for one full period before the end of a period37-6-5
Stored belongings after an orderLandlord may dispose after thirty days in listed cases55-3A-3(h)

Section 55-3A-1 does not itself list a separate pre-filing notice period for the three grounds. If a lease has its own notice terms, those can control, as discussed below. A landlord who is unsure which clock applies should ask the magistrate court clerk or an attorney before filing.

How does the no-cause termination notice work?

A landlord can end a month-to-month or other short periodic tenancy by giving notice for one full period before the end of a period. Section 37-6-5 says a tenancy from year to year may be ended by either party with written notice at least three months before the end of any year. A periodic tenancy with a period shorter than a year may be ended by that same notice or by notice for one full period before the end of any period.

Where the notice goes matters. When it is for the tenant, it may be served on the tenant or on anyone holding under the tenant, and the same is true of any part of the leased premises. A tenant's notice to the landlord can be served on the owner or the owner's agent.

Two carve-outs apply. The section does not apply where a special agreement fixes some other notice period or says no notice is to be given. Nor is notice needed for a tenant whose term ends at a certain time.

  • Year to year: written notice at least three months before year end.
  • Shorter periodic tenancy: notice for one full period.
  • Lease with its own terms: check the agreement first.
  • Fixed term ending on a set date: no notice needed under this section.

What happens at the hearing?

The court schedules a hearing five to ten judicial days after the petition is filed, and the landlord must serve notice of it right away. Section 55-3A-1(c) requires service under Rule 4 of the West Virginia Rules of Civil Procedure or by certified mail, return receipt requested. The notice tells the tenant that any written defense must be filed and served within five days of receiving it, and the petitioner then files the petition with proof of service.

If the tenant does not appear, answer or file a response by the hearing, section 55-3A-3(a) says the court shall enter an order granting immediate possession to the landlord. If the tenant answers, the hearing covers the issues raised. For a rent claim, the tenant can argue that the landlord breached a material covenant on which the duty to pay rent depends. For a breach or damage claim, the tenant can raise defenses to the petition.

Section 55-3A-2 adds that the tenant may assert any defense available in an action for ejectment or unlawful detainer.

Continuances are for cause only and cannot be granted to either party as a matter of right. If the tenant gets one, the tenant must pay into court any periodic rent that becomes due while it lasts.

How does the order and removal work?

If the court finds wrongful occupation, it enters an order granting immediate possession, and the order sets the date by which the tenant must leave. Section 55-3A-3(f) tells the court to consider the nature of the property, such as furnished or unfurnished, the possible harm to each side, and other relevant facts when setting the time to vacate.

The order also provides that if the tenant stays past that time, the sheriff shall forthwith remove the tenant, taking care to guard against damage to the property of both landlord and tenant. The statute names the sheriff as the one who removes the tenant.

On appeal, a tenant who wins gets money damages only if the lease term has expired, unless there is an issue of title, retaliatory eviction or breach of warranty. During an appeal, a tenant is not entitled to stay if the tenancy has otherwise expired.

What can a landlord do with belongings left behind?

The statute gives the landlord three options after a possession order when the tenant leaves belongings. Under section 55-3A-3(h), the landlord may dispose of items without liability if the tenant says in writing they are abandoned or if the items are garbage. The landlord may also remove and store the items, or leave them on the property.

  • Stored items may be disposed of after thirty days if the tenant has not paid reasonable storage and removal costs and has not taken the property back, or if storage costs equal the value of the items.
  • Items left on the property may be disposed of after thirty days if the tenant has not paid the reasonable cost of leaving them and has not retrieved them.
  • Items worth more than $300 must be stored for up to thirty more days if the tenant or a secured party says they intend to remove them and pays the reasonable costs.

Can you sell a house that has a tenant in it?

You can usually sell a rental while it is occupied, but a buyer who wants the house empty has to reckon with the timeline above. A petition, a hearing five to ten judicial days later, a possible defense, and then a vacate date set by the court all come before the sheriff can act.

That timeline affects how an owner thinks about a sale. A conventional buyer who needs a vacant house, or whose lender will not close with an occupant, may walk away from a rental with a pending case. We buy houses as-is, so ask us whether an occupied house is something we can take on.

We have not confirmed in a statute what happens to an existing lease when a landlord sells, so we do not state a rule here. Read your lease, and ask a West Virginia attorney whether it binds a new owner.

  • Gather the lease, rent ledger and any written notices.
  • Note whether the tenancy is year to year, periodic or for a fixed term.
  • Photograph any damage before and after the tenant leaves.
  • Keep copies of what you served, and how.

Where do you find the court forms?

The West Virginia Judiciary hosts the petition and a civil summons for wrongful occupation of residential rental property on its magistrate court forms page. The petition form includes a notice that any party seeking over $20.00 or possession of real estate may elect a jury trial, and that the election must be made in writing within 5 days of service in wrongful occupation cases or the right is lost.

More questions about West Virginia Eviction Notice Rules

How many days does a West Virginia landlord have to wait before filing an eviction?

Section 55-3A-1 does not set a separate waiting period for the three listed grounds: unpaid rent, breach of a warranty or leasehold covenant, and damage to the property. The hearing is set 5 to 10 judicial days after filing. Check your lease for notice terms of its own.

How long does a tenant have to respond to an eviction petition?

Five days. The notice of hearing tells the tenant that a written defense may be filed within five days of receiving it, and the magistrate court rules give a defendant 5 days after service of the summons and complaint to answer in wrongful occupation cases.

How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?

Notice for one full period before the end of a period. Under section 37-6-5, a periodic tenancy shorter than a year can be ended that way, and a year-to-year tenancy needs written notice at least three months before the end of any year. A special agreement in the lease can change the notice.

Can a landlord remove a tenant without a court order?

No. Under section 55-3A-3, the court's order sets the date to vacate, and if the tenant stays beyond it the sheriff removes the tenant. The sources we read describe removal as a court and sheriff process.

What happens to a tenant's belongings after an eviction order?

The landlord may dispose of items the tenant has declared abandoned in writing, or garbage. Otherwise the landlord may store the items or leave them in place, and may dispose of them after thirty days in the listed cases. Items worth more than $300 may need up to thirty more days of storage.
